Decision — rec and play

Status: accepted 2026-10-11. Amends the source layout (AGENTS.md §3.4).

The decision

  • One Rust command-line tool, cli/recplay, installed as rec and play. The binary is recplay. rec and play are links to it, added at install time in /opt/mixos/bin, and it chooses its behaviour from the name it was started as. Run as recplay, it prints help for both.
  • play puts something on the desktop.
    • A file or URI opens with the handler the desktop already knows. That means shared-mime-info for the type, desktop entries' MimeType= and mimeapps.list for the handler. MixOS ships no table of its own and names no application.
    • A .mix program is performed when the person runs play x.mix themselves.
    • An .mx document is read by its schema and never executed.
    • play has no media decoders. It describes and previews a foreign format only through a handler's own command-line tool, named in a per-user document that ships empty.
  • play is the one resolver.
    • play --serve answers play.open, play.resolve, play.info, play.handlers and play.perform on the Bus. The file manager and the portal's OpenURI use it, so every way of opening a file reaches the same handler.
    • Opening a .mix over the Bus shows it in the editor. Only play.perform runs it, and every perform is logged.
  • rec writes an editable Mix script from what happens on the desktop. It builds on executed commands, verb classes and the broker's observation stream. Runs of lines to one application are grouped in address … end, and a script never waits with a sleep.
  • A recording spec comes first. docs/docs/spec/recording/ is written and accepted before rec is built. It settles what these sources alone cannot:
    • Replay arguments. The broker does not show the payloads of a native session's calls, and a command event carries no arguments. Each application declares a recording surface: the committed actions it publishes with the arguments needed to repeat them, such as the path a dialog returned.
    • One record per action. A Bus call that runs a command shows up both in observation and as a command event. A causal identifier, or a rule for which source is authoritative, keeps exactly one.
    • Per-verb replay rules. Targets are resolved stably instead of being dropped (a tab, a buffer). Fencing values are made fresh on replay (revisions, operation ids). Deliberate waits such as ced.wait are kept as conditions, never turned into sleeps.
    • Sensitivity. Each owner marks what is sensitive, including text embedded in other values. A recording that lacks a required argument says so and is marked incomplete. It never guesses.
  • rec and play are accepted name collisions. Both names belong to sox, which installs /usr/bin/rec and /usr/bin/play (checked 2026-10-11 in Arch Linux and Debian trixie, where sox is the only owner).
    • MixOS installs to /opt/mixos/bin, which comes first in its PATH, so a MixOS session's play is this one.
    • sox's commands stay reachable by full path.
    • MixOS's own units and scripts call /opt/mixos/bin/play by absolute path.
    • recplay itself collides with nothing.

Why

Opening a file and recording what a person does are two halves of the same contract, the desktop's verbs. One resolver means the file manager, the portal, the command line and agents never disagree about which application opens a file. Using the freedesktop data that applications already install means MixOS learns a new format the moment an application that handles it is installed, without a MixOS change.

A recorded script is ordinary Mix. It can be read, edited, shared and performed on another machine, and it shows exactly how the work was done.

The two names are the plain words for the two actions. sox's tools of the same names are audio utilities that a MixOS session does not ship. The cost, calling them by full path, falls on few people and is easy to pay.

Consequences

  • AGENTS.md §3.4 lists the accepted collisions: mix (Elixir), and rec and play (sox).
  • play's Bus verbs, the per-user handler document and the Bus snapshot document schema are registered as contracts when they land.
  • The file manager stops spawning xdg-open and calls play.open.
  • Rejected: a MixOS MIME-to-application table. It duplicates what every application already installs, and it would have to name applications.
